channel.title: FONUR news
channel.description: News, fixtures, events and history for alumni and friends of Northeastern University Rugby, the Maddogs.

item.title: The Maddogs stay on top of the conference
item.description: A tight win over Iona, women continue their unscored on season.

item.title: Another big win for the boys: 75–0 over Princeton
item.description: A massive win over Princeton, the alumni gathering moves to the Babson match on October 24, and the defending national champion women open their season.

item.title: The boys are back
item.description: A 40–10 opening win over UConn, and the alumni are targeting the match against Iona.

item.title: Giving Day 2026, and both clubs head to the CRCs
item.description: Both clubs qualify for the CRC tournament. The men open their sevens season in Ireland, and the women win the first CRC qualifier hosted at Northeastern.

item.title: Thank you: over $10,000 raised
item.description: The men win two prizes in the Pack Gives Back, and set up the regular-season finale against BC for first place in the Liberty Conference.

item.title: The Pack Gives Back, and a salute to our alumni coaches
item.description: A fundraiser for the senior class and 2006–2025 grads, a thank-you to the men's alumni coaches, and the scores from two big weekends.

item.title: The Dogs keep rolling
item.description: More big wins at UMass Amherst: the women win 58–0 and the men 33–15.

item.title: Big wins for both clubs
item.description: The women beat BU 120–7 and the men win 69–0. Both clubs head to UMass Amherst this weekend.

item.title: The Maddogs partner with Geltman & Company
item.description: A new Instagram campaign with behind-the-scenes content and full coverage of the match against Brown.

item.title: The men's and women's fall schedules
item.description: The men open with a strong scrimmage against UNH. Old Boys, save October 4; Old Girls, save November 1.

item.title: This weekend: tailgate, the Free Jacks and the All-American gala
item.description: The schedule for Saturday, June 21: a tailgate at Pageant Field, the Free Jacks, the NCR All-Americans against Ballynahinch RFC, and the gala.

item.title: Remembering Steve Rice
item.description: An anchor of the pack through the late 80s and early 90s.

item.title: Introducing the Hall of Fame class of 2025
item.description: Five inductees, honored at the gala on June 21.

item.title: The Maddog women are CRC 7s national champions
item.description: Wins over Howard, Northern Iowa, Notre Dame and Iowa took the D1 club title, and Giving Day raised nearly $47,000.

item.title: A recruiting push, and Kourtney Bichotte-Dunner to Portugal
item.description: Coach Ed and Eric Graham visit an Ohio combine, and a Lady Maddog is picked for the NCR high-performance tour.

item.title: Spring alumni events, and another All-Star title for Coach Ed
item.description: The Hall of Fame weekend in June, a Free Jacks tailgate in May, and the Maddogs' Six Nations fantasy league.

item.title: A great season for the women's club
item.description: The women fall to #1 Wheeling in the final four after a brilliant season, and planning starts for the spring alumni weekend.

item.title: The women's defense takes down #2 Michigan
item.description: The Lady Dogs beat the two-time defending NCR D1 champions 32–26 to reach the final four.

item.title: The women's club rolls into the playoffs
item.description: An undefeated regular season, capped by a 57–0 win over BC. Today they take on UConn at Carter Field for a place at the regional championships.

item.title: Dogs get the win, and a call to young alumni
item.description: The Pack Gives Back asks 2014–2025 grads to step up, and the Maddogs bash SUNY Binghamton for their first win of the season.

item.title: Remembering Keith "Bubba" Salome
item.description: The criminal era lost a true giant.

item.title: Sarah Levy wins Olympic bronze, and a perfect tour of France
item.description: Lady Maddog alum Sarah Levy and USA Sevens win bronze in Paris, and the NCR All-Stars go 4–0 in France.

item.title: All-Americans to France, and a new arena for NU
item.description: Coach Ed leads NCR All-Americans on a tour of France, and Matthews Arena will be replaced.

item.title: Giving Day 2024: $14,601 for the men's club
item.description: Second place among 64 club teams, and a new effort to update the alumni contact list.

item.title: The 40th anniversary weekend
item.description: Tailgating at the Free Jacks, a dinner at the Alumni Center and an alumni match in the dome.

item.title: The Maddogs turn 40: anniversary weekend and a new alumni board
item.description: Save the date for March 16 and 17. Plus the new FONUR board, a coaching endowment, and congratulations to the women's club on a national title.

item.title: Men beat Nazareth; the women roll on
item.description: A 43–22 win gets the men off the mark, and the women beat BU 88–10.

item.title: A tough start, and great news from France
item.description: Losses to Fairfield and Dartmouth, and the Atlantic Coast All-Stars beat Sydney in Bordeaux.

item.title: Coach Ed to lead the Atlantic Coast All-Stars in Bordeaux
item.description: Ed Tubridy, Coleman Jackson and Alvaro Borrego head to the World University Rugby Invitational in France.

item.title: Spring wrap-up: the CRCs, and the women are national champions
item.description: The men won their CRC opener and pushed champions Kutztown close; the women won the D1 sevens title unbeaten.

item.title: Sevens results: Monumental Sevens and the Liberty Conference
item.description: Fifth at the Free Jacks' Monumental Sevens, then third and second at the Liberty Sevens at Fairfield.

item.title: The gala and touch tournament were a resounding success
item.description: Over 180 alumni, students and friends at the New England Aquarium, after the Memorial Touch Tournament returned.

item.title: Introducing the Hall of Fame class of 2023
item.description: Seven inductees, honored at the gala at the New England Aquarium on March 18.

item.title: A win over Wentworth, and the Dogs in LA
item.description: The young Dogs beat Wentworth on the old Triangle of Death, and the sevens squad played the LA stop of the World Sevens.

item.title: Coach Ed's All-Stars win in Houston again
item.description: For the second year running, Ed Tubridy's Liberty Conference Reds won the NCR all-star fifteens.

item.title: Bowl win over Fordham ends the fall
item.description: The Maddogs beat Fordham 44–22, and the young Dogs tested BC at Alumni Stadium.

item.title: A big win to finish the league season
item.description: The Maddogs took a season's worth of frustration out on Buffalo, 67–7.

item.title: A win at Harvard's 150th
item.description: After a loss at AIC, the Dogs beat Harvard 31–19, and the B side kept up its shutouts.

item.title: Fall 2022: a new coach and a grueling schedule
item.description: Former Free Jacks fullback Danny Collins joins the coaching staff.

item.title: Remembering Chris Scinto
item.description: Friends and teammates remember one of the toughest Maddogs.

item.title: Another season wrapped up
item.description: The CRCs in New Orleans, and congratulations to the class of 2022.

item.title: A Giving Day record, and a CRC invitation
item.description: Over $40,000 raised, both alumni challenges won, and an at-large bid to the CRCs.

item.title: Second at the CRC qualifier in Quincy
item.description: Wins over Fairfield, Iona and Harvard before falling to Kutztown in the final.

item.title: Winter update
item.description: Remembering Keith Hague, NCR All-Star champions in Houston, and Sarah Levy scores three at Twickenham.

item.title: Iona takes the final, and COVID ends the season
item.description: A 19–10 loss in the Liberty final, then the NCR quarter-final at Queens was cancelled.

item.title: Halloween monsoon: NU 20, Fordham 17
item.description: Two games these men will never forget: the Maddogs win the semi-final in a downpour, and the B side wins 48–10.

item.title: A lesson at Dartmouth, then 98–7 over UConn
item.description: After an 18–0 run in fifteens since 2018, the Dogs fell at Dartmouth, then finished the league season 6–1.

item.title: NU 50, BC 20
item.description: The Maddogs took care of BC, and now face their greatest challenge in recent memory at Dartmouth.

item.title: Unbeaten through four: Tufts, then Fairfield
item.description: A 53–7 win over Tufts and a hard-earned 22–13 win at Fairfield, and the B side's shutout streak.

item.title: Dogs take down URI
item.description: The Maddogs beat URI 42–14 and the second side won 22–0.

item.title: Hall of Famers celebrated in a 67–5 win over UMass
item.description: Back on the field after the pandemic, the Maddogs honored three new Hall of Famers at halftime.

item.title: Six new Hall of Fame inductees
item.description: Six inductees for the Hall of Fame class of 2022, a new athletic director who goes by "Maddog", and the fall schedule.

item.title: Liberty Eagles, coached by Ed Tubridy, win the first NCR tens
item.description: Five Maddogs played as two Liberty Conference sides met in the final in New Orleans.

item.title: Four Maddogs named to the New England All-Stars
item.description: Coach Tubridy leads the squad in New Orleans, and Giving Day raises $28,300 from 912 gifts.

item.title: A season of preparation
item.description: No matches this fall, but the Maddogs never stopped learning and growing.

item.title: Fall 2020 update
item.description: Remembering Jake Kennedy, virtual training through the pandemic, and the endowment reaches $160,000.

item.title: Update from the team: 19th in the country
item.description: An undefeated fifteens season, a Plate in LA, and a top-25 finish, from club president Jack Hale.

item.title: Coach Miccio's words to the team
item.description: The spring season ended early. Here's what Coach Alex Miccio told the boys.

item.title: Plate winners in Los Angeles
item.description: Four wins from five and 145 points to 26 at the Los Angeles Invitational.

item.title: Highs and lows
item.description: The alumni sponsor a new set of 35th-anniversary jerseys, and the club mourns one of its own.

item.title: 2019 Liberty Conference champions
item.description: The Maddogs beat BC in the final to win the Liberty Conference for the second time in three years.

item.title: Unbeaten regular season, AIC down, BC to go
item.description: The Maddogs beat UConn to finish 7–0, then beat AIC 25–14 in the Liberty Conference semi-final.

item.title: 6–0: the Dogs get it done in New York
item.description: Overcoming a halftime deficit and a yellow card, the Maddogs beat Fordham 31–17.

item.title: Maddogs 5–0
item.description: A 48–21 sweep of Tufts, and the B side is having a solid season too.

item.title: Maddogs are 4–0
item.description: A one-point win at UMass, 21–20, after a missed dropkick on the final play.

item.title: NU 42, BC 33
item.description: In front of a ferocious pack of NOBs at Alumni Weekend, the Maddogs took down BC under the lights.

item.title: Opening win on the new field at Carter
item.description: NU 63, URI 3, in the Maddogs' first-ever match at Carter Playground.

item.title: The 2019 fall campaign
item.description: An all-alumni support staff joins Coach Ed as the Maddogs chase a second Liberty title in three years.

item.title: Summer update: Alumni Weekend moves to October
item.description: BC under the Friday night lights at Carter Field, golf and the Hall of Fame banquet, October 4 and 5.

item.title: Maddogs win the Bowl at the National Sevens
item.description: Four straight wins on day two, ending with a last-play win over Cal Poly, gave NU ninth place in the country.

item.title: Maddogs head to 7s Nationals
item.description: Liberty Conference champions, the Dogs head to Tucson for the D1 National Sevens Championship.

item.title: A side wins the Liberty Sevens at URI
item.description: Wins over Tufts, UConn twice and Fairfield in the final earn the top seed for the conference final at AIC.

item.title: Plate winners in Las Vegas
item.description: The Maddogs brought home hardware from the Las Vegas Invitational for the first time in three years.

item.title: The first Maddog Memorial Touch Tournament
item.description: A new winter tradition in the Carter Field dome, honoring Michael "Strock" Strouch and Mike Walsh.

item.title: Winter gathering, and the Hall of Fame's second year
item.description: The first Memorial Touch Tournament on January 26, and the nominees for the second Hall of Fame team.

item.title: Maddogs finish the fall 4–2
item.description: Wins in the rain over Tufts and UConn, and a Liberty Bowl date with Fordham.

item.title: Senior night against Tufts
item.description: After a gut-wrenching loss at BC and a trip to Fairfield, the Dogs honor their seniors at Parsons.

item.title: A heartbreaker against UMass; BC next at Alumni Stadium
item.description: The Dogs head to BC on October 6, and the B side plays the first official game at the new Carter Field.

item.title: NU 69, URI 0
item.description: A shutout at URI to open the Liberty season, and the B side won 44–0.

item.title: Fall 2018 schedule
item.description: Circle October 6 at BC, and two Saturday-night home games under the lights at Parsons.

item.title: Voting opens for the first Maddog Hall of Fame
item.description: The inaugural class will be inducted at the Alumni Weekend banquet on May 12.

item.title: Sevens season: unbeaten at Babson, then Vegas
item.description: The Maddogs won the Babson tournament without conceding a try, and chase a Nationals bid through the Liberty series.

item.title: Winter gathering, and Alumni Weekend moves to May
item.description: The first ten years of Maddog rugby turned out for the winter dinner. Alumni Weekend is May 11 and 12.

item.title: Back on top: the 2017 Maddogs finish 8–0
item.description: Liberty Conference New England Division champions, and a 42–10 bowl win over SUNY Cortland.

item.title: Maddogs beat BC
item.description: A try and conversion at the death gave the Dogs a 20–17 win, their first over BC since 2012.

item.title: Maddogs power to a 2–0 start
item.description: Wins over URI, 41–16, and UMass, 37–17, set up a big test against Boston College.

item.title: Fall 2017 schedule
item.description: Endicott, then the first Liberty Conference season, with home games at Parsons Field.

item.title: Alumni match: Dogs 29, NOBs 24
item.description: The undergrads outlasted the NOBs in the heat, and the push to complete the endowment begins.

item.title: Bob Hubbard and the first Maddog team
item.description: Founding father Bob Hubbard sent a photo of the first Maddog side, ahead of a hoped-for return to Boston.

item.title: Maddogs wrap up the spring, and join a new conference
item.description: A 26–7–2 sevens record, Carter Field under construction, and a new home in the Liberty Conference.

item.title: Spring update: the endowment and the Maddogs in Vegas
item.description: The activation deadline is extended to June 2018, and the sevens squad heads to the Las Vegas Invitational.

item.title: Maddogs end 2016 with a big win
item.description: A 75–7 win over Brockport in the ECRC–Empire Challenge, and a push to activate the Wallin Endowment.

item.title: Maddogs host UConn to close the fall
item.description: Friday night at Parsons, the Dogs get one last chance to go out as winners.

item.title: Rugby season is here
item.description: The 2016 Maddogs open against Harvard and host Phil Ciccarelli's UMass at Parsons.

item.title: Alumni Weekend 2016: golf, the Sox and the alumni match
item.description: Golf at Brookline, Red Sox vs Blue Jays and the alumni match at Parsons Field, June 3 and 4.
